relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-setting-alternate-address
relations.evidence: This command is used to set the alternate address for a node. This alternate address allows the node to be connected by a different address, this is useful when an external agent tries to connect via a NAT'd environment such as the cloud or kubernetes.

notable_absence.finding: The Alternate Ports table names every service by product-facing name (Cluster Manager, Data, View Engine, Query, Search, Analytics, Eventing, Backup) and both the plaintext and TLS port for each, but nowhere on the page is there any statement of which RBAC role or privilege is required to run --set/--remove versus --list - the only permission language anywhere on the page is the generic boilerplate 'If you do not have a user account with permission to execute the command then it will fail with an unauthorized error', shared verbatim with every other setting-* page in this batch. Given that alternate-address reconfiguration is a cluster-topology-affecting operation (it changes how external agents reach a node), the complete absence of a named role citation is a sharper gap here than on lower-stakes settings pages.

cross_component_finding: The Alternate Ports table's Description column uses UI-facing service names ('Cluster Manager', 'View Engine', 'Search') interchangeably with the port-name-only style used elsewhere on the same table row (e.g. 'kv', 'cbas', 'eventingAdminPort'), and with terse fragments like 'Used by the SDKs and XDCR' and 'Used by the SDKs to query data' repeated almost verbatim for different services (kv/capi both say 'Used by the SDKs and XDCR to transfer data' / 'Used by the SDKs and XDCR' with only the object of the sentence changing) - a flag-description-copy-paste-across-siblings pattern consistent with this round's authorship-provenance hypothesis, here inside a single table rather than across sibling pages.
cross_product_finding: N/A on this page directly; the alternate-address mechanism (NAT'd/Kubernetes external connectivity) has no Capella analogue evidenced here since Capella manages its own network topology - no cross-product claim is made.
